## Type

Bug Fix

## Caveats (if any)

<!-- caveats round 4 of 4 -->

### High

- Shadow eval passed the effort to the shadow model, fixed in `afb8eb7dfe`
- `task_budget` without `thinking` got Bedrock's 400, fixed in `ce02ebfbd0`

### Medium

- An ARN with `model_info.base_model` lost the effort under `drop_params`, fixed in `afb8eb7dfe`
- No live row covered `reasoning_effort_levels`, added at `afb8eb7dfe`
- No live run covers the ARN paths, since the QA role gets AccessDenied
- An ARN behind `litellm_proxy` got the effort, fixed in `14145a88c5`

### Low

- Converse Claude now answers 400 to an effort it can't take, as intended
- Under `drop_params` a malformed effort now drops with a 200, but `reasoning_effort` still gets 400
- Haiku 4.5's `xhigh` or `max` gets Bedrock's 400 text in place of LiteLLM's

<details>
<summary>Details and evidence</summary>

High, shadow eval

The shadow eval logger replays a sampled `/v1/messages` request through the same adapter with the logged model, then passes the translated keys to `router.acompletion` for the shadow model, which is the auto-router under evaluation or a fixed baseline model. At `731bbed432` a Converse Claude request with `output_config.effort` and no `thinking` handed the shadow call `output_config={"effort": "high"}`, where the merge base handed it none, and an OpenAI shadow model gets that field as is in its request body. `afb8eb7dfe` kept `output_config` out of the shadow call unless the request has `thinking`, which is what the merge base did (Decision 8), and since `14145a88c5` the adapter does that itself, since the shadow translation names no provider. `test_anthropic_arm_sends_a_bedrock_claude_effort_to_the_shadow_model_only_with_thinking[no_thinking]` fails at `731bbed432` and passes at the tip, and its `thinking` case keeps the effort

High, `task_budget`

/live-pr-risk at `afb8eb7dfe` found that every `output_config` key but `format` went to Converse without `thinking`, so `{"effort": "low", "task_budget": {"type": "tokens", "total": 20000}}` went from 200 at the merge base to Bedrock's 400 `output_config.task_budget: Extra inputs are not permitted`, with or without `drop_params` and the beta header. `ce02ebfbd0` sends only `effort` without `thinking`, and every key but `format` with it, as the merge base did (Decision 2). The QA rows `m_task_budget` and `m_task_budget_only` answer 200 on both legs, and `test_bedrock_converse_claude_without_a_thinking_block_gets_only_the_effort_from_output_config` fails at `afb8eb7dfe` and passes at the tip

Medium, ARN with `model_info.base_model`

At `731bbed432` the adapter handler read only the top-level `base_model` call kwarg, while `completion()` falls back to `model_info.base_model` and Converse gates an ARN's effort on that value. So an ARN deployment with `model_info: {base_model: us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8}`, `drop_params: true` and no `thinking` sent no `output_config`, and the warning asked for a `base_model` that was already set. `afb8eb7dfe` reads `base_model` in the handler the way `completion()` does, and Decision 6 now names both places. The adapter test case `[no_thinking_drop_params_model_info_base_model]` fails at `731bbed432` with `assert None == {'effort': 'high'}` and passes at the tip

Medium, declared levels

The proof had no deployment with `model_info.reasoning_effort_levels`. The table above now has one (Sonnet 4.6 declaring `low`, `medium` and `high`) against real Bedrock. `xhigh` gets 200 there, where the plain Sonnet 4.6 deployment gets the 400 for a tier it can't take, so the effort is rounded onto the declared levels before the check. At the merge base both get 200 because the effort never reached Bedrock

Medium, ARN behind `litellm_proxy`

/live-pr-risk at `33155467b0`, the same change on a merge of main, found that a `litellm_proxy/arn:aws:bedrock:...` deployment counted as a Bedrock Claude target, because the check reads only the model string, so `/v1/messages` with an effort and no `thinking` sent `output_config` to the next hop, where the merge base sent none. A `bogus` effort through a chained LiteLLM went from 200 to the inner hop's 400. `14145a88c5` sends the effort without `thinking` only through the `bedrock` provider (Decision 4). The QA rows `m_chain_arn_low` and `m_chain_arn_bogus` chain the proxy to itself through that ARN name and answer 200 on both legs, and `test_a_bedrock_arn_behind_another_provider_gets_no_effort_without_a_thinking_block` fails at `ce02ebfbd0` and passes at the tip. With `thinking` the effort still goes as at the merge base

Medium, no live ARN run

The only role on the QA node gets AccessDenied on CreateInferenceProfile and on Converse to the account's one application inference profile, and the role that can create one is not reachable from that node. Captured request bodies match the merge base for an ARN with `thinking` under global, request, or no `drop_params`, and for an ARN with no `base_model` and no `thinking` under `drop_params`. The new ARN requests are an effort without `thinking` and without `drop_params`, and one under `drop_params` with `base_model` set in `litellm_params` or `model_info`, and these now carry `output_config` the way the named Claude ids in the table do. A live run of those cases and of the `thinking` plus `drop_params` case closes this

Low

The intentional 200 to 400 follows the `drop_params` convention and is not severe. The old 200 ignored the effort, the new 400 is Bedrock's own answer or matches it (a direct Converse call with `xhigh` on Sonnet 4.6 gets `This model does not support effort level 'xhigh'`), and `drop_params` at any level keeps the 200. QA rows `m_haiku_effort`, `m_s46_xhigh`, `m_s46_list` and `m_effort_bogus` go from 200 to 400, and the `drop_params` rows stay 200 or go from 400 to 200. A non-string effort gets the same 400 or drop, where it used to be ignored without `thinking` and crash with a 500 with it

Under `drop_params`, `output_config: {"effort": "bogus"}` on `/v1/chat/completions` and on `/v1/messages` with `thinking` went from LiteLLM's 400 to a 200 that drops the effort with a warning, and so do `""`, `"High"` and a streamed request. That is the `drop_params` convention (Decision 5). The top-level `reasoning_effort: "bogus"` still gets a 400 under `drop_params`, which this PR leaves alone, so fixing it here would widen the PR to another carrier for no gain on this ticket

Haiku 4.5 takes no effort, so its `xhigh` or `max` on `/v1/chat/completions` and on `/v1/messages` with `thinking` now reaches Bedrock and gets `This model does not support the effort parameter`, where the merge base answered LiteLLM's `effort='xhigh' is not supported by this model` without the call. `high` already reached Bedrock at the merge base. The status stays 400 and `drop_params` drops it, so a second check before the call would add code for no change a caller can act on

</details>

## Final Attestation

- [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

issue.title: fix(proxy): resolve a team wildcard deployment for a wildcard key on files, batches and RAG routes
issue.body:
A key whose model allowlist is itself a wildcard, like `gpt-*`, skipped its team's own `openai/*` deployment on `/v1/files`, `/v1/batches` and `/v1/rag`, so those calls ran on the proxy's `OPENAI_API_KEY` instead of the team's key. Chat from the same key already used the team's key, and a key allowed `openai/*` or exact model names worked everywhere

Now a wildcard key and a wildcard team deployment count as overlapping when some model litellm knows for that provider matches both, the same way chat auth matches them. So a `gpt-*` key gets the team's `openai/*` key, and a `claude-*` key still never does

<details>
<summary>Original</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- `gpt-*` keys ran files, batches, and RAG on the proxy's OpenAI key
- Uploads and vector stores landed in the proxy owner's OpenAI project

How it solves it:

- Two wildcards match when a known provider model fits both
- Same matcher chat auth uses, so other providers stay closed

## User Flow

Before: a team developer whose key is allowed `gpt-*` gets their files and vector stores on the proxy's OpenAI account, or a 401 when that key is unset or wrong

1. The admin adds a team model `openai/*` holding the team's own OpenAI key, then gives the developer a team key allowed `gpt-*`
2. POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with a GPT model answers 200 on the team's key
3. POST https://litellm-domain/v1/rag/ingest, POST or GET https://litellm-domain/v1/files, and POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches run on the proxy's `OPENAI_API_KEY` instead, here a 401 "Incorrect API key provided: sk-proxy...-key"
4. Anything those calls do create lands in the proxy owner's OpenAI project, not the team's

After: the same calls run on the team's own OpenAI key

1. The admin adds a team model `openai/*` holding the team's own OpenAI key, then gives the developer a team key allowed `gpt-*`
2. POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with a GPT model answers 200 on the team's key
3. POST https://litellm-domain/v1/rag/ingest, POST or GET https://litellm-domain/v1/files, and POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches answer 200 on the team's key
4. A key allowed only `claude-*` in the same team still cannot use the team's OpenAI key on those routes

## Affected release

Regression in v1.96.0 for `GET /v1/files`, which used the team's key on v1.95.1. The other routes first used team keys later, so for them this is a bug in new behavior

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Both legs ran one curl flow on real OpenAI through two proxies with 2 workers each, sharing Postgres and Redis, alternating requests. The proxy's `OPENAI_API_KEY` is a placeholder, so a 401 naming `sk-proxy...-key` means it skipped the team key. [This gist](https://gist.github.com/mateo-berri/223a03eb2a96286d0027b687c543f21b) holds every whole output

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `gpt-*` key, file upload | 401 placeholder | 200 |
| `gpt-*` key, 5 other files routes | 401 placeholder | 200 |
| `gpt-*` key, RAG ingest and query | 401 placeholder | 200, "teal" |
| `gpt-*` key, batch create, get, cancel | 401 placeholder | 200 |
| `gpt-*` key, batch list | 200 | 200 |
| `gpt-*` key with 1 TPM, batch | 401 placeholder | 429, 9 tokens |
| `claude-*` key, files and RAG | 401 placeholder | 401 placeholder |
| Chat, exact and `openai/*` keys | 200 | 200 |

<details>
<summary>Shared setup</summary>

Both proxies run this config with `--num_workers 2` and `OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-proxy-env-fallback-not-the-team-key`. `$LEG/batch.jsonl` is [one chat request](https://gist.github.com/mateo-berri/223a03eb2a96286d0027b687c543f21b#file-after-batch-jsonl) to `gpt-6-luna`

```yaml
model_list: []
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
  store_model_in_db: true
router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: <port>
files_settings:
  - custom_llm_provider: openai
```

The admin then runs these on P1 (after leg shown, the before leg ran the same calls):

1. Create the team

   ```bash
   curl -s $P1/team/new -H "Authorization: Bearer $MK" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"team_alias":"wildcard-team-creds-qa"}' -w "\nHTTP %{http_code}\n"
   ```

   HTTP 200 ([whole output](https://gist.github.com/mateo-berri/223a03eb2a96286d0027b687c543f21b#file-after-01_team_new_mk-txt))

2. Add the team model `openai/*` with the team's real OpenAI key

   ```bash
   python3 - "$TK" "$T" <<'PY' | curl -s $P1/model/new -H "Authorization: Bearer $MK" -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data-binary @- -w "\nHTTP %{http_code}\n"
   import json,sys
   print(json.dumps({"model_name":"openai/*","litellm_params":{"model":"openai/*","api_key":sys.argv[1]},"model_info":{"team_id":sys.argv[2]}}))
   PY
   ```

   HTTP 200 ([whole output](https://gist.github.com/mateo-berri/223a03eb2a96286d0027b687c543f21b#file-after-02_model_new_mk-txt))

3. Create key A, allowed `gpt-*`

   ```bash
   curl -s $P1/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $MK" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"key_alias":"wildcard-gpt-key","team_id":"2a11de6a-1993-413b-90b7-743430ad7bbc","models":["gpt-*"]}' -w "\nHTTP %{http_code}\n"
   ```

   HTTP 200 ([whole output](https://gist.github.com/mateo-berri/223a03eb2a96286d0027b687c543f21b#file-after-04_key_generate_a-txt))

4. Create key B, allowed `gpt-6-luna`

   ```bash
   curl -s $P1/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $MK" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"key_alias":"exact-key","team_id":"2a11de6a-1993-413b-90b7-743430ad7bbc","models":["gpt-6-luna"]}' -w "\nHTTP %{http_code}\n"
   ```

   HTTP 200 ([whole output](https://gist.github.com/mateo-berri/223a03eb2a96286d0027b687c543f21b#file-after-04_key_generate_b-txt))

5. Create key C, allowed `openai/*`

   ```bash
   curl -s $P1/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $MK" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"key_alias":"provider-wildcard-key","team_id":"2a11de6a-1993-413b-90b7-743430ad7bbc","models":["openai/*"]}' -w "\nHTTP %{http_code}\n"
   ```

   HTTP 200 ([whole output](https://gist.github.com/mateo-berri/223a03eb2a96286d0027b687c543f21b#file-after-04_key_generate_c-txt))

6. Create key D, allowed `claude-*`

   ```bash
   curl -s $P1/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $MK" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"key_alias":"wildcard-claude-key","team_id":"2a11de6a-1993-413b-90b7-743430ad7bbc","models":["claude-*"]}' -w "\nHTTP %{http_code}\n"
   ```

   HTTP 200 ([whole output](https://gist.github.com/mateo-berri/223a03eb2a96286d0027b687c543f21b#file-after-04_key_generate_d-txt))

7. Create key E, allowed `gpt-*`, 1 TPM

   ```bash
   curl -s $P1/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $MK" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"key_alias":"wildcard-gpt-limited-key","team_id":"2a11de6a-1993-413b-90b7-743430ad7bbc","models":["gpt-*"],"tpm_limit":1,"rpm_limit":1000}' -w "\nHTTP %{http_code}\n"
   ```

   HTTP 200 ([whole output](https://gist.github.com/mateo-berri/223a03eb2a96286d0027b687c543f21b#file-after-04_key_generate_e-txt))

</details>

### Before (a66dc50efb)

#### Key allowed `gpt-*` uploads a batch file

1. Upload a batch file with key A

   ```bash
   curl -s $P1/v1/files -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_A" -F purpose=batch -F custom_llm_provider=openai -F "file=@$LEG/batch.jsonl;type=application/jsonl" -w "\nHTTP %{http_code}\n"
   ```

2. Observed

   ```
   {"error":{"message":"Error code: 401 - {'error': {'message': 'Incorrect API key provided: sk-proxy**************************-key. You can find your API key at https://platform.openai.com/account/api-keys.', 'type': 'invalid_request_error', 'code': 'invalid_api_key', 'param': None}, 'status': 401}","type":"invalid_request_error","param":null,"code":"401"}}
   HTTP 401
   ```

#### Key allowed `gpt-*` on the other files routes

<details>
<summary>Steps</summary>

1. Key A (`gpt-*`), `POST /openai/v1/files` on P2


   HTTP 200, `"status":"validating"` ([whole output](https://gist.github.com/mateo-berri/223a03eb2a96286d0027b687c543f21b#file-after-24_batches_create_p2_b-txt))

</details>

Also seen on the run, none caused or changed by this PR:

- Batch routes label upstream 401 and 429 `internal_server_error`
- `GET /v1/files` lists nothing right after fresh uploads
- Batch limiter lets through a batch whose file it cannot read
- The batch 429 message shows the key's hashed token

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix
✅ Test

<details>
<summary>Decisions</summary>

1. Which model names count as a match for two wildcards. I picked the models litellm knows for the route's provider, since the router can only infer a provider for a bare name it knows, so that is exactly the set chat could route there. A pure string overlap of the two patterns was the alternative, but it misses `gpt-*` against `openai/*` (no shared prefix) and would not apply provider inference the way auth does. A prefix overlap that is not in the known list (say `azure/prod-*` against `azure/*`) is already covered by the existing one-sided check
2. Speed. A cheap regex pass on the bare and `provider/` spelling picks candidates before the full auth matcher confirms each one, which took the no-match case from about 2 to 9 ms down to about 0.1 to 0.2 ms over the 212 known OpenAI models. A model it filters out only fails closed (no team key). I did not add a cache, since the provider's model list is read live and so can never be stale
3. Unchanged on purpose. Exact names, one-sided wildcards, and the all-proxy-models and all-team-models sentinels behave as before, and a non-wildcard key or deployment name never reaches the new check

</details>

## Final Attestation

- [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>
